_comment: Formal risk-event taxonomy for the hypervelocity-risk-sim spoke. Each entry is a failure-mode the simulator replays. Provenance is split at the right granularity: the scenario failure-mode TOPOLOGY (lag accumulates from a producer-minus-consumer rate deficit, error rates spike, releases cascade) is source_derived from public failure-mode reporting, but the specific numeric SHAPE PARAMETERS (degradation depth, phase timing, catch-up rate) are operator_calibrated — tuned, not from any cited source. The spreadsheet-vs-signal response-time gap the sim reports is likewise operator_calibrated ILLUSTRATION, not measured telemetry. The spoke keeps this reviewed taxonomy; packages/kri-taxonomy/crosswalk.yaml maps it onto the canonical hub catalog.

risk_events.name: Consumer-Lag Cascade
risk_events.description: Consumer lag accumulates from a sustained producer-minus-consumer rate deficit during a volume surge (a slow partition / rebalance); the payments domain's error rate spikes and an availability SLO violations. A capacity/observability gap that becomes an availability incident.

risk_events.name: Change-Induced Cascade
risk_events.description: A bad release propagates across interdependent services, tripping circuit breakers and forcing emergency rollbacks. Change failure surfaces as an availability and incident-recovery event.
frameworks: DORA / DevOps Research & Assessment (change failure rate)

risk_events.name: Transaction-Velocity Surge / Fraud-Control Response
risk_events.description: Transaction rate spikes to a multiple of baseline, tripping fraud detection that also blocks legitimate traffic. The elevated-velocity signal is routed to an AML review queue for human disposition — a simulated fraud-control signal, NOT a BSA/AML determination. A decision-quality and human-oversight risk where one signal must route to fraud and compliance teams with different SLAs.
risk_events.scope_note: The simulator makes no BSA/AML compliance assertion. A transactions-per-second surge is a fraud-control signal, not a money-laundering typology; the AML element models only routing to a human review queue. SAR/CTR determinations (31 CFR 1020) are out of scope.
frameworks: EU AI Act Art. 14 (human oversight) — applies only if the fraud decisioning is high-risk under Annex III

risk_events.name: Identity-Plane Lockout
risk_events.description: The customer identity/session plane degrades then fails: token issuance collapses, customers are locked out of accounts and funds in real time, and support saturates. The defining feature is the RECURSION — workforce SSO shares the failed plane, so responders are locked out of their own tooling with the customers (Meta 2021-10-04 class). Detection is near-instant in both regimes; ACCESS is the bottleneck. Break-glass restores tool access, then recovery arrives as a re-auth surge. Anchors: Auth0 global outage 2021-04-20; the 2021-01 brokerage login failures under volume; Meta workforce lockout 2021-10-04.
risk_events.scope_note: The simulator models availability and access mechanics only — no fraud, ATO or credential-stuffing determination is made; degraded-verification abuse is the rac dependency layer's blindness mode, priced there, not replayed here.
frameworks: FFIEC AIO — resilience of authentication infrastructure
